description: Focaccia Genovese is a true masterpiece of Ligurian baking, celebrated for its irresistibly soft, airy crumb and golden, dimpled crust. Infused with aromatic rosemary and bathed in rich olive oil, each bite transports you to the sun-drenched coasts of Genoa. This authentic recipe promises a delightful balance of savory flavors and a wonderfully satisfying texture, perfect as an appetizer or side.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough Starter
instructions.text: In a large bowl, dissolve the fresh yeast (or active dry yeast) in the warm water. Add 100g of the flour and stir until a smooth, thin batter forms. Cover with a clean cloth and let it rest for 15 minutes until slightly foamy.

instructions.title: Mix and Knead the Dough
instructions.text: Add the remaining 400g of flour and the fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons (30ml) of the extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 10-15 minutes until it is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Lightly oil a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or a clean kitchen towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Shape and Dimple
instructions.text: Gently punch down the dough to release the air. Transfer it to a well-oiled 9x13 inch (23x33 cm) baking pan. Gently stretch the dough to fill the pan, being careful not to tear it. Use your fingertips to create deep indentations all over the surface of the dough.

instructions.title: Second Proofing and Topping
instructions.text: Drizzle the remaining 2 tablespoons (30ml) of olive oil generously over the dimpled focaccia. Sprinkle the chopped fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt evenly over the top. Cover the pan loosely with plastic wrap and let it rise again in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffy.

instructions.title: Bake the Focaccia
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 220C (425F). Bake the focaccia for 20-30 minutes, or until golden brown on top and cooked through. The internal temperature should be around 90-95C (195-205F).

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Once baked, remove the focaccia from the oven and carefully transfer it to a wire rack to cool slightly. For an extra touch of flavor, you can drizzle a little more fresh olive oil over the warm focaccia before serving. Slice and enjoy warm or at room temperature.

tips: For the best texture, use strong bread flour (tipo 00 if available) as its higher protein content develops better gluten.
Do not rush the proofing stages; a slow rise develops superior flavor and a more airy crumb.
Serve focaccia warm, perhaps with a side of good quality extra virgin olive oil for dipping, or as an accompaniment to soups and salads.
article:
Focaccia Genovese, a cornerstone of Italian baking, is more than just bread; it's a culinary experience. Hailing from the picturesque Ligurian coast, this flatbread stands out with its signature dimpled surface, generous olive oil sheen, and a delicate balance of crispy crust and airy, chewy interior. When infused with fragrant rosemary, it transforms into a symphony of flavors that evokes the sun-drenched landscapes of Italy. If you've ever dreamt of recreating authentic Italian bakery aromas in your own kitchen, mastering Focaccia Genovese with rosemary and olive oil is an immensely rewarding journey. This article will guide you through the history, ingredients, techniques, and tips to bake a focaccia that will transport your taste buds straight to Genoa.

## What is Focaccia Genovese?
At its heart, Focaccia Genovese is a traditional Ligurian flatbread, renowned for its distinct character. Unlike other focaccia varieties that might be thicker or more cake-like, the Genovese version is typically thinner, with a delicate, slightly crisp crust and an interior that is remarkably soft and airy, riddled with small, irregular holes. Its surface is famously dimpled, a technique that creates small pools of golden extra virgin olive oil and allows for a perfect distribution of coarse sea salt and fresh rosemary. The key to its unparalleled flavor lies in the quality and quantity of extra virgin olive oil used, both in the dough and generously drizzled over the top before baking. This simple yet sophisticated bread is a testament to the Italian philosophy of letting high-quality ingredients shine, creating a staple that is equally at home on a breakfast table, as an accompaniment to a meal, or as a delightful snack on its own. The authentic Focaccia Genovese truly embodies the essence of Ligurian cuisine.

## Ingredients You Need
Crafting the perfect Focaccia Genovese requires a handful of high-quality ingredients. Each plays a crucial role in achieving that signature texture and flavor:

*   **Strong Bread Flour (Type 0 or 00):** This flour has a higher protein content, which is essential for developing strong gluten networks, resulting in the desired chewy texture and open crumb.
*   **Warm Water:** Around 105-115°F (40-46°C) is ideal for activating the yeast without killing it.
*   **Active Dry Yeast or Instant Yeast:** The leavening agent that gives the focaccia its rise and airy structure.
*   **Fine Sea Salt:** Essential for flavor and controlling yeast activity.
*   **Sugar (optional, a pinch):** A small amount of sugar can help activate the yeast and add a touch of sweetness, though traditional Focaccia Genovese is not sweet.
*   **High-Quality Extra Virgin Olive Oil:** This is non-negotiable. It contributes immense flavor, moisture, and a tender crumb. Don't skimp here; it's the soul of Focaccia Genovese.
*   **Fresh Rosemary:** Stripped from the stem and roughly chopped, it provides the iconic aromatic note. Dried rosemary can be used in a pinch, but fresh is vastly superior.
*   **Coarse Sea Salt (e.g., Maldon, flaky salt):** Sprinkled on top, it provides bursts of briny flavor and a pleasant textural crunch.

## Step-by-Step Instructions
Making Focaccia Genovese is a process that rewards patience and attention to detail.

1.  **Activate the Yeast:** In a large bowl, combine the warm water, yeast, and a pinch of sugar (if using). Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy, indicating the yeast is active.
2.  **Form the Dough:** Add the flour and fine sea salt to the yeast mixture. Drizzle in about 2 tablespoons of extra virgin olive oil. Mix with a wooden spoon or your hands until a shaggy dough forms.
3.  **Knead:** Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Knead for 8-10 minutes until it's smooth, elastic, and no longer sticky. Alternatively, use a stand mixer with a dough hook for 6-8 minutes. The dough should be quite soft and hydrated.
4.  **First Rise (Bulk Fermentation):** Lightly grease a clean bowl with olive oil. Place the dough in the bowl, turning it once to coat. Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until doubled in size.
5.  **Prepare the Pan:** Liberally coat a 9x13-inch (or similar size) baking pan with extra virgin olive oil. This prevents sticking and contributes to the crispy bottom crust.
6.  **Stretch the Dough:** Gently deflate the risen dough and transfer it to the prepared pan. Using your olive-oiled fingertips, gently press and stretch the dough to fill the pan. It might resist at first; if so, cover it and let it rest for 10-15 minutes, then continue stretching. Aim for an even thickness.
7.  **Second Rise (Proofing):** Cover the pan with plastic wrap or a damp towel and let the dough rise for another 30-45 minutes, or until noticeably puffy. Preheat your oven to 425°F (220°C) towards the end of this rise.
8.  **Dimple and Season:** Once risen, remove the cover. Using your olive-oiled fingertips, firmly press into the dough to create deep dimples across the entire surface. Don't be shy; you want to go almost all the way to the bottom of the pan. Drizzle another generous amount of extra virgin olive oil over the dimpled dough, ensuring it pools in the depressions. Sprinkle evenly with fresh rosemary and coarse sea salt.
9.  **Bake:** Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the focaccia is golden brown on top and the bottom is cooked through and crisp.
10. **Cool:** Once baked, immediately transfer the focaccia from the pan to a wire rack to cool slightly. Serve warm or at room temperature.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results
Achieving bakery-quality Focaccia Genovese is within reach with a few expert insights:

*   **Embrace High Hydration:** Focaccia dough is typically very wet. Don't be tempted to add too much extra flour during kneading. A high hydration level is key to a light, airy, and chewy crumb. If the dough is too sticky, oil your hands instead of adding flour.
*   **Quality Olive Oil is Paramount:** As mentioned, extra virgin olive oil is not just an ingredient; it's a flavor enhancer and a textural component. Use a good quality, fruity olive oil for maximum impact. Drizzle generously, especially over the dimples.
*   **Don't Fear the Dimples:** The dimpling process is crucial. It prevents the focaccia from puffing up like a regular bread loaf, creates pockets for the olive oil and salt, and contributes to the characteristic texture. Press firmly, almost to the bottom of the pan.
*   **Warm Environment for Rising:** Yeast thrives in warmth. A slightly warm, draft-free spot will ensure your dough rises properly and develops good flavor.
*   **Hot Oven, Quick Bake:** A high oven temperature ensures a rapid rise and a beautifully crisp crust without drying out the interior.
*   **Listen to Your Dough:** Dough often tells you what it needs. If it's resisting stretching, give it a few minutes to relax. If it's not rising, your environment might be too cold or your yeast might be old.
*   **Fresh Herbs Make a Difference:** While dried herbs can work, fresh rosemary provides an incomparable aroma and flavor that elevates the Focaccia Genovese experience significantly.

## Serving Suggestions
The beauty of Focaccia Genovese lies in its versatility. It can be enjoyed in countless ways:

*   **As an Appetizer:** Serve warm with a side of good quality balsamic vinegar for dipping, or with a selection of olives and marinated artichokes.
*   **With Charcuterie and Cheese:** Its simple flavor profile makes it a perfect companion for cured meats like prosciutto or salami, and a variety of cheeses.
*   **Alongside Meals:** It's an excellent bread to serve with Italian stews, hearty soups, or fresh salads, perfect for soaking up delicious sauces.
*   **For Sandwiches:** Slice it horizontally and fill with your favorite deli meats, cheeses, roasted vegetables, or a simple caprese salad for a truly gourmet sandwich.
*   **Breakfast or Snack:** Enjoy a slice with your morning coffee, or as a light snack throughout the day. The rosemary and olive oil notes are surprisingly delightful any time.
*   **Plain and Simple:** Sometimes, the best way to enjoy it is warm, straight from the oven, appreciating its pure, unadulterated flavor.

## Variations and Substitutions
While the classic Focaccia Genovese with rosemary and olive oil is perfect as is, there are many ways to experiment and adapt it to your taste:

*   **Other Herbs:** While rosemary is traditional, you can substitute or add other fresh herbs like thyme, oregano, or a mix of Italian herbs.
*   **Onion and Garlic:** Thinly sliced red onion or finely minced garlic can be pressed into the dimples along with the rosemary for an added layer of savory flavor.
*   **Cherry Tomatoes:** Halved cherry tomatoes, gently pressed into the dough before baking, add a burst of sweetness and juiciness.
*   **Olives:** Pitted Kalamata or green olives can be scattered over the surface for a briny touch.
*   **Cheese:** A sprinkling of grated Parmesan or crumbled feta can be added in the last few minutes of baking for a cheesy crust.
*   **Chili Flakes:** For a touch of heat, sprinkle a few red pepper flakes over the top.
*   **Gluten-Free Flour:** While the texture will be different, you can experiment with gluten-free bread flour blends. Ensure the blend contains xanthan gum for elasticity.
*   **Brine Topping:** Some authentic recipes involve pouring a light salt brine (water, salt, olive oil) over the dimpled surface instead of just olive oil and coarse salt. This creates an even more intensely flavorful and slightly crispier crust.

Baking your own Focaccia Genovese with rosemary and olive oil is a journey into the heart of Italian baking. From the careful selection of ingredients to the patient kneading and proofing, each step contributes to a bread that is both humble and exquisitely flavorful. The aroma filling your kitchen will be a reward in itself, and the first bite will confirm that you've mastered a true classic. So, roll up your sleeves, embrace the olive oil, and prepare to delight your senses with this iconic Ligurian masterpiece. Buon appetito!
